answer: Push Square’s launch review reports a 30 FPS target and no Performance option on the PS5 Pro copy it tested. In the same article, Rockstar’s Marc Chambers attributes higher-frame-rate limits on PS5 Pro to the game’s simulation workload and says the team used the upgraded GPU and upscaling for visual fidelity. sections: Read the frame target and frame stability separately

FPS is a rate. Dividing 1,000 milliseconds by that rate gives the time available per frame. A target of 30 corresponds to approximately 33.3 ms. At 60, it is about 16.7 ms. Why a GPU improvement can still matter at 30 FPS

Rockstar’s account says the team put the additional graphics capability toward fidelity and identified CPU simulation as a constraint on increasing this title’s target. The next check is a matched comparison at the same location, weather and camera angle. A higher image-quality setting and a higher frame target are different outcomes. [psPro] [launchInterview]

If you already own the game, record the installed version and the options visible on your own hardware. A new menu entry needs a measured test to establish what it delivers under load. Record Windows available physical memory and committed memory with your editor, browser and usual background tasks open. Run a local model during the same workload. Measure through prompt processing and generation. Record the model tag, context and CPU/GPU split with ollama ps. Read the entire system’s physical pressure before adding up memory reported by separate processes, because views can overlap. Repeat with the largest prompt you actually need. Ollama documents that parallel requests increase context allocation, so run a separate concurrency case if several processes share your service. [faq]
Watch both physical pressure and the Windows commit limit

Microsoft describes the system commit limit as backed by RAM and page files. A successful allocation does not mean all of that memory stayed in RAM. Correlate slowing requests with sustained low available memory and paging activity. A single hard page fault can reflect a file being read from storage. Look for repeated changes that coincide with the actual slowdown. [pageFile]
Read the budget as an observation, not a model requirement

In the illustration, background use occupies 11 GiB and the observed incremental local workload adds 17 GiB at the same moment, leaving about 4 GiB in a simplified 32 GiB physical budget. If the next workload adds another 6 GiB at that same peak, the example asks for 34 GiB. Those are hypothetical deltas, not estimates for every 32B model. With the same quantization and background workload, compare a smaller context or fewer simultaneous requests first. More RAM may address repeated physical pressure. If placement is already entirely on the GPU and slowdown comes from that device, hold the RAM purchase until your evidence identifies a host bottleneck. [faq] [pageFile]

title: Does DDR5 memory speed matter for CPU-only local LLMs?
description: Estimate theoretical desktop DDR5 bandwidth, then measure model prompt and generation rates before paying for faster memory.
answer: DDR5 rate can matter when CPU inference is limited by reading model data from system memory. It cannot establish a tokens-per-second gain by itself. sections: Calculate the ceiling using the populated channels

Two 64-bit memory channels move a theoretical 16 bytes across both channels per transfer. Multiplying 5,600 million transfers per second by 16 gives 89.6 decimal GB/s. At 3,600 MT/s it gives 57.6 GB/s. This simple data-width model covers the combined data paths, not effective application throughput. Check the CPU’s supported speed for the number of modules and ranks it uses. [ryzen9950] [popRules]
Keep the model fit and CPU path fixed

Check that the workload stays in system RAM without heavy paging and that both tests use the same model, context and thread settings. Run enough repetitions to separate loading from generation. Compare a prompt-processing case and a generation case rather than assuming they stress the hardware in one way. [cpuBench] [api]
Buy memory only for a demonstrated limit

If faster supported memory changes sustained generation but the setup still meets your goal, value the time it saves. If adding capacity prevents paging, that may be more important than transfer rate. If GPU offload is possible for your intended model, test that as a separate system option. [faq]

description: Measure repository, SDK, container and WSL disk growth. Add room for simultaneous builds and model files before choosing SSD capacity.

sections: Recalculate what the summary means

The total time in this illustrative capture is 1.1 seconds. Divide 100 frames by that duration for about 90.9 FPS. Under a nearest-rank convention, the 99th percentile frame time is the 99th item after sorting from short to long, which is 20 ms. group: RAM, STORAGE, COOLING & PRACTICAL HARDWARE QUESTIONS
title: 16 GB vs 32 GB RAM for gaming: test your real background load
description: Compare repeatable game runs with your normal background apps, then distinguish system RAM, dedicated VRAM and game settings before buying a kit.
answer: 16 GB can work when your game and normal apps fit in available system memory. Compare the same game scene with normal background apps and with an otherwise quiet desktop. If the busy case repeatedly shows low available RAM, paging and slow frame intervals, investigate capacity before replacing the GPU. A game’s published RAM floor and dedicated GPU memory requirement describe separate resources. [gameRamTest] [cod7] [pageFile]

visual.title: Use two runs to separate pressure from coincidence
rows: Same game, map and settings with everyday apps

sections: Keep the game workload unchanged

Choose a repeatable scene and record the patch, resolution, textures and frame limit. Capture several passes in each background condition so shader compilation and first-run loading do not dominate one case. Check the publisher’s target configuration. A published minimum does not include every background app you use. [cod7] [gameRamTest]
Look for physical RAM pressure at the same moment

Record available system memory, committed memory and paging activity. Check GPU memory separately. Microsoft distinguishes physical memory and the commit limit backed partly by page files. Pressure across the whole system matters more than a single large process reading. If game textures alone reproduce the issue while system memory has headroom, test GPU behavior separately. [pageFile]
Change capacity without introducing a new variable unnoticed

If a larger kit is warranted, verify its compatibility and compare at the same game settings. DDR speed, timings and channel population can change with a kit replacement. Record them before attributing the result entirely to capacity. Use your measured result to decide whether 32 GB is worth the upgrade.
actions: Check memory choices for the actual motherboard

title: Why Ollama unloads models when you switch: would more RAM help?
description: Separate keep-alive timing, load limits, GPU headroom and parallel context when two local models will not stay loaded together.
answer: Ollama can unload an idle model after its keep-alive period or unload models to free memory for another request. It also has limits on how many models may stay loaded, provided they fit. More system RAM can help a host-memory bottleneck, but cannot raise the dedicated VRAM budget for GPU-resident models or change a configured load limit. [faq] [api]

rows: Run a request and inspect residency
Switch within the configured retention period
Record whether it loads again or stays warm

sections: Test scheduling before capacity

Use two named model tags, a fixed context and a short gap between requests. Check ollama ps after each request. Compare the result with a run that waits beyond the intended retention interval. The generate API documents keep_alive for the request. Verify your actual runtime configuration before interpreting a reload as insufficient system RAM. [faq] [api]
Check which memory would need to increase

Ollama documents that concurrency increases context memory demand. Test one parallel request per model first and record placement. If the second model cannot coexist while both are on GPU, record available VRAM. If the intended placements rely on system RAM, measure available host memory at the point of failure. A host upgrade cannot directly add VRAM to a discrete GPU. [faq] [context]
Change one setting at a time

Try a smaller context or artifact and check whether both models stay loaded without loss of acceptable output. If switching is infrequent, the time spent reloading may be cheaper than an upgrade. If a proven memory bottleneck repeats during real work, compare the cost of a larger host kit or card for the exact resource that is short.

answer: No. AMD lists two memory channels for the Ryzen 9 9950X. Adding four sticks on a supported four-slot board can populate two DIMMs per channel. title: DDR5-5600 CL28 vs DDR5-6000 CL36: Calculate CAS Delay
description: Convert memory timings to nanoseconds and see how higher bandwidth can come with a longer first CAS delay.
answer: DDR5-5600 CL28 gives 10 ns of CAS delay, while DDR5-6000 CL36 gives 12 ns. These are calculated timing values. The 6000 kit has the higher nominal transfer rate. Actual workload performance requires a matched test. [cas]

visual.title: Two kits with different advantages
rows: Hold CPU, timings and workload visible

sections: Use data rate rather than oscillator frequency

The label is in MT/s. Double-data-rate memory transfers twice per clock cycle, so a cycle takes 2000 divided by data rate in nanoseconds. Multiplying by CL gives the delay for that timing under the stated running profile. [cas]
Keep other timings visible

CAS describes one step. A row change can also involve precharge and row-to-column delay. This is why a smaller CL in nanoseconds does not on its own predict an FPS uplift. For a purchase, compare the full timings, capacity and exact workload evidence. [kingstonDecoder]
Verify the profile on your system

Find the kit part number, motherboard support and intended profile before buying. Confirm the measured running data rate after setup. If a more ambitious profile forces looser settings or is unstable on the system, use the stable settings to redo the calculation. [popRules] [amdExpo]

title: Does DirectStorage Mean You Need a Faster NVMe SSD?
description: Check game support and the Windows feature requirements, then compare actual loading before paying for more SSD bandwidth.
answer: Check whether the game uses DirectStorage and meets its own requirements. Microsoft’s Windows feature sheet lists an NVMe drive with the standard controller driver and a compatible DirectX 12 GPU with Shader Model 6.0. A newer PCIe generation alone supplies no evidence that the title loads meaningfully faster. [directStorage] [storageRequired]

visual.title: A game-specific upgrade decision
rows: Replay the same load on matched systems

sections: Look for the game’s installation guidance

Check the publisher version and PC requirements first. An SSD requirement says where to install the game. A DirectStorage implementation says something about how the game handles reads. Keep both facts with the title and build number. [directStorage] [cyberpunk]
Know what the API changes

Microsoft documents a path for many smaller reads with reduced CPU overhead. Sequential drive speed on the box describes a different test from loading a game scene. A faster drive can still help workflows that move large files, which is a separate reason to buy it. [directStorage]
Run a repeatable test

Record the same scene, game version and platform settings. Time repeated loads, distinguish first launch from warm-cache repeats, and log both before applying an upgrade recommendation. Check usable capacity alongside the result so the purchase fixes the actual problem.

title: 1 TB vs 2 TB SSD for gaming: calculate your installed library
description: Convert advertised capacity to the units your PC uses and budget separately for the active library, patches and free space.
answer: A marketed 1 TB is about 931 GiB before formatting and reservations. A marketed 2 TB is about 1,863 GiB. Use one unit when adding your operating system if applicable, currently installed games, other simultaneous installs and free space needed for updates. If your typical peak exceeds the usable capacity of the 1 TB model, price the 2 TB option. [storageUnits] [cod7]

visual.title: One made-up single-drive requirement before buying

sections: Put real installation sizes in one unit

Drive packaging normally uses powers of ten. Divide bytes by 1,073,741,824 to convert to GiB. Some software displays a binary value with a GB label, so check what the screen means before adding figures. Measure actual installed size after optional packs and captures if they share the drive. [storageUnits]
Distinguish permanent installs from free space a game requests

Activision’s Black Ops 7 requirements give an SSD available-space figure at launch. An available-space requirement is not a guarantee of the exact occupied size after future patches. Use current installed values for games you have and record publisher estimates as separate planning figures when the actual files are unavailable. Confirm peak free-space prompts during an update. [cod7]
Make the two options comparable

The example asks for 980 GiB before considering formatting, so one nominal 1 TB drive cannot meet it. A 2 TB option has more raw space if the supported formatted volume still meets your need. If you already have a second suitable drive, split the worksheet by volume instead of pooling space that cannot serve an individual installation.
actions: Check SSD interface and fit before ordering

description: Identify the SSD protocol and exact slot on the MSI MAG B550 TOMAHAWK before changing firmware or trying to initialize a drive.
answer: Check the SSD protocol before assuming the drive failed. On MSI’s exact MAG B550 TOMAHAWK, the specifications list SATA support for M2_1 and list PCIe for the chipset-connected M2_2. A SATA M.2 drive in a PCIe-only slot can be physically seated without a supported data link. Read the SSD label and the motherboard specification for your exact model. [b550] [msiDetection]

rows: Use a slot explicitly supporting SATA
Read M2_1 conditions on this board

M.2 describes the physical form factor. Read the drive’s manufacturer part number for SATA or PCIe, then review the slot’s protocol and length support. The exact board model matters. An MSI B550 model with a related name can have a different connection map. For the matching board, read notes about other slots or devices that may share connections. [b550]
Probe a supported combination with the PC powered down

Follow the manufacturer’s safe device installation steps. If another slot explicitly supports your protocol and physical size, test there and note what else is installed. If supported combinations still do not detect the SSD, use MSI’s documented isolation tests or a known-good enclosure that explicitly supports the drive’s protocol. Check the manufacturer’s support path before flashing firmware just to try a guess. [msiDetection]
Separate detection from boot and formatting

A recognized drive can still lack a valid boot setup or mounted volume. Recheck firmware storage information before changing partitions. If the drive contains data, avoid initializing or formatting it as a detection test. Work through the correct next step based on whether firmware, boot or the operating system cannot find it.

title: Is a Hard Drive Still Worth Buying? Budget for a Backup You Can Restore
description: Choose bulk storage for a second copy, then test recovery and account for offline or off-site needs.
answer: A hard drive can be a practical choice for bulk backup when capacity and cost matter more than interactive speed. Keep an independent copy and test a restore. Moving the only copy to an external drive reduces space pressure without creating a backup. [seagateBackup] [seagateRestore]

Plan for more than a drive failure

Keep an independent copy and account for site loss, accidental deletions and other failures. Seagate’s overview explains the 3-2-1 approach. Choose a separate location or service consistent with your recovery needs. [seagateBackup]

title: Measure GPU Clearance in an Already Assembled PC

Record the card’s complete envelope

Use the exact board SKU, including the cooler and connector orientation. Avoid relying on the GPU chip name. Plan around the assembly path

Check side panel lips, removable brackets and the insertion angle. For a tight upgrade, use an unpowered dry fit or confirm dimensions with the case maker. Retain the measurements with the saved build, because moving a radiator or storage cage changes the result.

group: RAM, STORAGE, COOLING & PRACTICAL HARDWARE QUESTIONS
title: What do 80 PLUS Bronze and Gold mean for wall power?
description: Read the 115 V desktop efficiency table and calculate AC input at one load. Separate the certification threshold from measured electricity use.
answer: For 115 V internal non-redundant power supplies, 80 PLUS Bronze requires 85% efficiency at half rated load and Gold requires 90%. At the same 325 W DC output for two 650 W PSUs, those threshold efficiencies correspond to about 382 W and 361 W AC input. The comparison is a calculation at the published thresholds. Each actual PSU can behave differently. [efficiency]

visual.title: Where the input power goes in the rounded Gold example

table.title: 115 V internal non-redundant minimum efficiency for these tiers

sections: Start with a fixed DC load

Divide the DC output by efficiency as a decimal to estimate AC input. For the example, 325 ÷ 0.85 is about 382.4 W, and 325 ÷ 0.90 is about 361.1 W. The roughly 21 W difference applies to the two threshold examples at the same load. At 60 hours of that exact workload the difference amounts to about 1.27 kWh. Idle and peak use would need their own load measurements and durations. [efficiency]
Use the exact report and voltage category

Look for your exact model on the certification site. Read its test report, including the voltage category and the results at each load point. Do not take an efficiency number from one voltage category and assign it to a different product or supply condition. A 325 W output is half load for a 650 W unit, but less than half load for an 850 W unit. Select equivalent load conditions for the decision you are making. [certification] [efficiency]
Keep component fit and power quality in the buying decision

An efficiency threshold tells you how much input power is needed for a specified output condition. Check capacity, connectors, physical fit and independent PSU testing separately. If electricity cost is the deciding factor, measure your system under its actual work before extrapolating the example to a year. A wall reading measures the input for the entire system attached to the meter, so make sure your comparison uses the same devices.

description: Distinguish the custom processor’s documented accelerator blocks from withheld clocks, core counts and desktop GPU equivalence.

title: Does Nintendo Switch 2 use DLSS? Read the game and display evidence
description: Switch 2 supports NVIDIA DLSS. Learn how to distinguish a game’s render resolution, reconstruction and HDMI output before comparing modes.
answer: Yes. NVIDIA confirms that the Nintendo Switch 2 processor includes Tensor Cores for DLSS upscaling. For any individual game, check the version, mode and evidence of reconstruction. Nintendo’s published TV limits describe what the console can send to the display. A TV showing a 4K signal alone does not tell you the resolution rendered by the game. [switchChip] [switchSpec]

sections: Read the console output limits together

Nintendo specifies TV output at up to 3840 × 2160 at 60 fps, with 120 fps output supported at 1920 × 1080 or 2560 × 1440. The built-in screen is 1920 × 1080. A headline that lists 4K and 120 together can hide that the stated maximum resolution and stated maximum frame rate apply under different conditions. [switchSpec]
Ask for game-specific proof

Record the full game title, patch and handheld or docked mode. Look for a developer statement about DLSS. If only a technical analysis is available, check how it identified the method and how it counted internal pixels. Keep the console output setting and a measured game frame rate in separate rows. A result for one title or patch does not establish support for a different one. [switchChip]
Use a mode comparison to choose your display

On the display you own, compare modes using the same scene and game patch. Pay attention to visible detail, motion stability and responsiveness. A 4K input can be worthwhile even when the internal frame is smaller. A game capped below 120 fps does not acquire a faster simulation just by selecting a 120 Hz output. Hardware support is the starting point for this comparison, and the game determines which mode is available. [switchSpec]

title: Why Console Games Target 30 or 60 FPS: The Frame Budget
description: Translate FPS into milliseconds and keep the game’s render target separate from the display’s refresh rate.
answer: At 30 FPS, frames are spaced about 33.33 ms apart. At 60 FPS, the target is 16.67 ms. A studio may reduce graphics work or tune scene complexity to make the shorter interval sustainable. The TV’s refresh rate is a separate setting. [psModes] [psVrr]

visual.title: Frame interval at three targets

sections: Apply the shorter deadline to the whole workload

Simulation, command submission, graphics work and presentation must sustain the cadence. A studio can tune shadows, resolution or ray tracing for a specific title, while the mode still needs enough CPU and GPU time in its heaviest scenes. Read the developer’s stated target for that patch. [psModes]
Separate a 120 Hz signal from 120 unique frames

At a steady 120 Hz a 30 FPS cadence can repeat each frame for four refreshes. The equivalent for 40 FPS is three. These are arithmetic examples for evenly paced frames at fixed refresh. VRR can change the display timing, subject to console, game and display support. [psVrr]
Look for stability as well as a peak

Identify the mode and use a consistent game scene. A useful performance report states the patch, console, target and observed drops. If a label promises 60 FPS, prioritize evidence about delivery through busy gameplay rather than a single fast scene. [psModes]

Separate placement from cooling and power effects

Try a shorter context, a smaller model or a different quantization individually. Record if each still produces acceptable output.
